passages.stem: The school invention fair opened at nine. A group of pupils made a robot that could move small blocks. They tested it carefully and changed two parts before the visitors arrived. Their teacher praised the teamwork and asked everyone to explain their work clearly. This was important for their project.

A second group prepared a photo exhibition about the invention fair. They used a camera to record the stages of each project. The photographs showed first attempts, mistakes and final improvements. Visitors liked seeing how an idea could become better with patient work. This was important for their project.

At the end of the fair, the pupils wrote short reflections in a shared notebook. They described what they learned and how they would improve next time. Their teacher collected the notes and promised to display the best advice on a classroom wall. This was important for their project.

activities.passage:
From: noura@school.example
To: rashid@school.example
Subject: Plans for our class project
Dear Rashid,
I hope you are enjoying your week. Our class is organising a invention fair at the school hall next Monday. We will meet at nine in the morning near the main entrance. Our teacher asked each group to prepare one small display and explain it to visiting parents. My group will bring a robot and a poster showing how we made our project. Please bring your notebook, some drinking water and a reusable bag. We do not need to buy new decorations because the school has plenty of materials we can use again. The event finishes at one o'clock. After that, we will tidy the area and return our equipment to the classroom. I hope you can come and help us. Please reply before Sunday.
Best wishes,
Noura

passages.stem: Students visited the coast to learn about marine life. They carried notebooks and drew animals they saw in the water. Their guide explained that shells should stay on the beach because small creatures sometimes need them. Everyone followed the rules and kept the area clean.

A second team observed boats near the shore. They noted the shapes and counted how many people were on each boat. The teacher reminded pupils to stay away from the edge of the water. Later, the group discussed how to make safe choices outdoors. This was important for their project.

After lunch, the children shared their photographs and notes. Some pupils had pictures of fish, while others had drawings of plants that grew near the sand. Each group made a small poster explaining one new fact about the coast. They were proud of their discoveries.

passages.stem: At the neighbourhood market, volunteers prepared a stall for fresh local fruit. They arranged apples carefully and put prices on the table. They asked customers to use reusable bags. Most families agreed because they wanted to create less rubbish in the area. This was important for their project.

Near the bakery, a group of pupils sold small cakes for a charity project. They wrote the ingredients beside each cake to help visitors choose. A teacher checked their calculations and helped them count the money. The students learned how careful planning supports good teamwork.

In the afternoon, visitors shared ideas about improving the market. Some wanted more shade and others suggested drinking-water stations. The pupils collected the suggestions in a notebook and promised to discuss them in class. They also thanked the shopkeepers for their friendly help. This was important for their project.

Asma

Laila: It will take place at the park on Thursday. Our teachers prepared activities for families. Interviewer: Who is helping you organise the event? Laila: My friend Yousuf is helping me, and classmates are arranging tables. Interviewer: What will visitors see first? Laila: They will see a display about a paintbrush. We made it in class. Interviewer: What should visitors bring? Laila: They should bring a reusable water bottle and a notebook. We want to avoid waste. Interviewer: Thank you for sharing your plan. Laila: You are welcome. Interviewer: What did you learn from this experience? Laila: I learned to listen to others, check my work and make better plans. Working together is important because each person has a useful idea.

passages.stem: The art class visited a public park on Thursday morning. Pupils brought paper, pencils and paintbrushes to record what they could see. Their teacher asked them to observe shapes and patterns before drawing. Many students chose flowers and trees near the pathway. This was important for their project.

Another group interviewed people about the colours they liked in public spaces. They listened carefully and wrote short notes. A local artist demonstrated how to draw a simple boat. The pupils practised the steps and compared their first attempts with their final pictures. This was important for their project.

Before leaving the park, everyone displayed their work on a long table. Each child described one decision and one difficulty. The teacher encouraged them to give kind, specific feedback. Later, the pupils carried their pictures back to school and planned a small exhibition. This was important for their project.
